h2: Pool Equipment Nusa Dua – Pumps, Filters & Salt Systems
intro: Keeping pool equipment in Nusa Dua running smoothly matters even more than inland — coastal air accelerates corrosion on fittings while Bukit water leaves scale inside pumps and filters. Whether you manage a villa in Tanjung Benoa or a gated estate in Bualu, Bali Fix handles installation, repair and balancing of the full system so your water stays crystal-clear for guests.

sections.h3: Why Coastal Conditions Wear Down Your System Faster
sections.text: The combination of salty sea breeze and mineral-heavy Bukit tap water creates a tough environment for any mechanical part near your pool. In coastal pockets like Sawangan, we regularly find corroded multiport valves, limescale clogging impeller housings, and cracked O-rings well before their normal service life. A pump that hums quietly in Ubud can develop a grinding noise here within a single dry season. Catching these signs early means a small parts swap instead of a full unit replacement.

sections.h3: Typical Repairs We Handle Across Nusa Dua Villas
sections.text: Most calls from villa owners and managers involve one of five issues: a pump that won't prime after the rainy season, a sand filter due for media replacement, a multiport valve leaking at the handle, a salt chlorinator cell throwing error codes, or underwater lights flickering and tripping the RCD. In resort-standard properties guests spot every drip and every cloudy afternoon, so each fix gets a hotel-level finish — clean connections, properly torqued fittings, and a test cycle before we leave.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp Before Booking a Visit
sections.text: Before scheduling a visit, send two or three clear photos on WhatsApp: the pump nameplate showing model and serial, the filter housing with its multiport valve position visible, and any error display on your chlorinator controller. If you're inside a gated complex around Bualu, include the gate code or security contact so our technician can coordinate entry in advance. Cost depends entirely on what the inspection reveals — once we see the photos we'll give you a straightforward quote right there in the chat.

sections.h3: Prevention Tips for Large Pools and Overflow Systems
sections.text: Large pools with overflow edges and water features demand more than a weekly chemical top-up. Check your auto-fill float monthly for debris, listen to the pump at startup for any whine that wasn't there last month, and wipe down salt-cell plates every two weeks during peak season. Humid coastal air will pit even stainless fittings if left unattended. A short preventive visit twice a year keeps your system from failing mid-stay when guests are watching.

faq.q: Do I need to arrange gate access before a technician enters my estate?
faq.a: Most complexes around Nusa Dua require pre-approved visitor lists. Send us your security contact or gate code on WhatsApp when booking so our technician arrives at the right time without waiting at the gate.

faq.q: Is a salt chlorinator better for a villa pool than regular chlorine tablets?
faq.a: Salt systems produce gentler water and cut daily chemical handling, but they still need periodic cell cleaning and salinity checks. We install and service both types; the best fit depends on your pool size and how often guests use it.

faq.q: How often should a large overflow pool get its equipment inspected?
faq.a: Twice a year is a sensible minimum for larger pools with overflow edges and water features. Between visits, watch for rising energy bills, a pump that sounds different, or persistent cloudiness after backwashing — any of those are good reasons for a quick WhatsApp check-in.
